the course of renal failure in rats with a unilateral nephrectomy and a contralateral subtotal nephrectomy is accelerated by the addition of urea to the diet.
uremia is associated with a decrease in glomerular filtration rate, and that the increase in plasma urea concentration is a factor in the development of renal failure.

the effect of urea supplementation to a low-protein, low-phosphorus diet on the course of renal failure in rats with a 5/6 subtotal nephrectomy.
the effect of high urea concentrations on the course of chronic uremia in rats.
the role of high plasma urea concentrations in renal failure progression in rats.

uremia is not a simple consequence of renal failure but a cause of renal failure progression.
high blood ureas are the most important cause of the progression of renal failure.
high plasma urea concentrations are a cause of intravascular hemodynamic disturbances in the course of experimental renal failure.
